newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi oil delayed by electric fault - Turk agency.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil delayed by electric fault - Turk agency.

text.p: The planned flow of oil from Iraq to Turkey on Tuesday under the U.N. oil-for-food plan was delayed by an electric fault in the Iraqi oil city of Kirkuk, Turkey's Anatolian news agency said.
It quoted an official from the Turkish pipeline company Botas as saying that the pumping of oil from Kirkuk to the southern Turkish port of Ceyhan would be delayed by one to two hours.
Botas officials were not immediately available for comment and it was not clear from the agency report whether oil had started flowing from Kirkuk. Iraq had said it would start pumping at 0500 GMT.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said earlier Iraq would pump 650,000 barrels through its pipeline to Turkey on Tuesday.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited exports of oil under an oil-for-food deal for Iraqis suffering under economic sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

Under the U.N. plan, concluded in May but held up by disputes over implementation, Iraq will be able to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.
